clinical_diagnosis_summary: The patient presents with post-rotator cuff surgery shoulder pain and secondary cervical discomfort due to prolonged sitting. This kinetic chain circuit addresses the primary glenohumeral joint dysfunction (Protocol 1), integrates scapulohumeral rhythm and proximal stability (Protocol 5), and anchors the entire kinetic chain with axial postural control of the cervical spine (Protocol 3). This sequential approach aims to restore optimal shoulder function while mitigating compensatory patterns originating from the neck.
precautions: Avoid active pain provocation. Maintain controlled movement velocities, focusing on smooth, deliberate execution. Ensure scapular depression and retraction are maintained during Protocol 1 and 5 to prevent compensatory upper trapezius dominance. For Protocol 3, focus on gentle chin tucks and thoracic extension without neck hyperextension.

exercises.clinical_rationale: Directly addresses glenohumeral joint mobility and strength post-surgery, focusing on abduction within a pain-free range and without compensatory scapular elevation.
Enhances scapulohumeral rhythm and promotes synergistic activation of the rotator cuff and periscapular muscles, crucial for stable overhead activities and supporting glenohumeral function.

Establishes a stable axial postural anchor by strengthening deep neck flexors and improving thoracic mobility, directly counteracting the effects of prolonged sitting and providing a stable base for upper extremity function.
